gaps: UniFi Access and Talk have no official spec
Cloud write access through the connector proven only for one hotspot voucher create and delete on one test console

novel_features.name: Path and capability probe
novel_features.description: See which transports and products answer on each console. Write status is yes, no or unproven, and a probe alone never reports yes.
novel_features.rationale: Combines every surface and both transports into one per-console verdict.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this first in a session to learn what answers before planning a change. Spends one read per surface per console.

novel_features.name: Impact and lockout check
novel_features.description: Estimate from the last sync what a proposed action would take down and whether it risks your way back in. It never reports safe.
novel_features.rationale: Joins mirrored devices, clients, cameras and WANs against the control path.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before any change that could cut the path needed to undo it. Verdicts are blocks-path, at-risk, no-known-risk or cannot-determine, and it cannot see every cause of path loss.

novel_features.name: Journaled change with undo
novel_features.description: Send one change to an official Network or Protect path with a journaled before-image, a read-back check and undo. Nothing is sent without --confirm.
novel_features.rationale: Needs a local journal linking before-image, mutation and read-back.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use instead of a plain write when the change must be checked and revertible. Docs say cloud keys are read-only today, other cloud writes are unproven beyond one voucher create and delete, and --trial expiry is unverified.

novel_features.name: Config drift
novel_features.description: See field-level config changes between two synced snapshots, marked attributed (in the change journal) or out-of-band.
novel_features.rationale: Needs console-keyed snapshots joined to the change journal.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to answer what changed in config and whether it went through change apply. Needs at least two syncs.

novel_features.name: What happened since I looked
novel_features.description: One timeline, built from local syncs, of state changes, ISP dips, drift, newcomers and journaled changes.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local join across products and snapshots.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for a catch-up summary instead of querying each product. A flap between two syncs is missed.

novel_features.name: Newcomer detection
novel_features.description: List clients, devices and cameras first seen at a sync in a window.
novel_features.rationale: The API has no first-seen field; only local history knows.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to spot unfamiliar hardware. Randomized MACs can inflate the list, and a visit between syncs is missed.

novel_features.name: Firewall rule prediction
novel_features.description: Predict which firewall policy would match a hypothetical packet. This is a local prediction with no API confirmation.
novel_features.rationale: No API simulate endpoint exists; evaluated locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before editing rules. Treat indeterminate as unknown; legacy firewall rules are outside the model.

novel_features.name: Device topology tree
novel_features.description: See gateway, switches and APs as a tree per console, from the last sync.
novel_features.rationale: Computed from parent links in the mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to orient on the physical layout. Uplinks come from per-device detail requests, so sync --no-hydrate leaves the tree flat.

narrative.headline: Operate UniFi consoles through the cloud connector or your LAN, with a local history, change previews and a change journal.
narrative.value_prop: One binary for the official UniFi APIs, over the cloud connector or a direct connection to your gateway. A local mirror keeps a snapshot from each sync, and 'impact' estimates what a change would affect before you make it. Reads have run against one test console over the cloud connector; most writes have not.
narrative.auth_narrative: Cloud: create a key at unifi.ui.com under Settings > API Keys and set UNIFI_API_KEY. Local: create a key in the Network app under Settings > Control Plane > Integrations, set UNIFI_LOCAL_API_KEY, and pass --gateway or set UNIFI_GATEWAY. The keys are separate, and a cloud key is never sent to a gateway. Run 'reach' to see what answers.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the binary runs. Sends no requests.
See which consoles, products and transports answer. Needs a key.
Build the local mirror and take a snapshot. History features need it.
Read the timeline. Changes show up once there is more than one sync.

troubleshoots.fix: A console page means the path missed the API. Check the route with doctor and run reach. Pass --gateway as a bare host: the CLI adds /proxy itself and rejects a path.
Several consoles are visible, or none. Choose one with --console or UNIFI_CONSOLE_ID, or use --gateway.
Cloud keys are not sent to a gateway. Create a key in the Network app under Settings > Control Plane > Integrations.

troubleshoots.symptom: 401, 403 or 405 on a write through the connector
troubleshoots.fix: Docs say cloud keys are read-only today. Try --gateway with a local key; local writes are also untested live.

troubleshoots.symptom: 403 not the owner of the host
troubleshoots.fix: Non-organization keys reach only the key owner's consoles; use the owner's key or an organization key.
The connector limits requests to 25 seconds; narrow the query. A write may still have applied and is not replayed, so read state first.
The connector documents 100 requests per minute per console. The CLI paces itself per process, so parallel runs can exceed it; wait for Retry-After.

troubleshoots.symptom: Response too large through the connector
troubleshoots.fix: The connector caps responses at 10 MB. Page with --limit and --offset, or use --gateway.
UNIFI_READ_ONLY is set, so writes are refused. Unset it to write; --dry-run still works.
Add the console id to the comma-separated list, or target an allowed console.

narrative.when_to_use: Use for operating UniFi consoles over the cloud connector or a local gateway: health, config review, device and guest actions, Protect, and what-changed questions from local snapshots. Run 'impact' before, and prefer 'change apply' for, changes that could affect connectivity. Start with reads: cloud writes are unproven and no route has been tested live.
anti_triggers: UniFi Access or Talk administration: no official API here and no commands cover them
Blocking a client with an official command: the API offers only guest authorize and unauthorize, so blocking means an unverified raw controller path or a firewall or ACL rule
Proving a firewall outcome: rule-predict is a prediction with no API confirmation
Live video streaming beyond handing out RTSPS links
First-time console setup and account administration

recipes.title: Check before changing
recipes.explanation: Reports affected clients and a control-path verdict from the last sync. Run sync first, or the verdict is cannot-determine.

recipes.title: Narrow device output
recipes.explanation: Keeps large device payloads small for agents. Get the site id from network list-sites.

recipes.title: Attribute changes
recipes.explanation: Marks each change attributed when the change journal holds it, otherwise out-of-band. Writes made outside change apply count as out-of-band.

recipes.title: Test a local route
recipes.explanation: Probes the gateway with UNIFI_LOCAL_API_KEY. Works without a cloud key.

recipes.title: Preview a journaled change
recipes.explanation: Prints the plan and sends nothing. Add --confirm to send it.

trigger_phrases: what would restarting this unifi device affect
